chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):

Major ritual ablution (ghusl) is required in seventeen places: the night of the seventeenth of Ramadan, which is the night of the meeting of the two armies at Badr; the night of the nineteenth, on which the delegation of the year is recorded; the night of the twenty-first, on which the trustees of the prophets died, Jesus son of Mary was raised, and Moses was taken (died); the night of the twenty-third, in which the Night of Power is hoped for. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah al-Basri said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Perform ghusl on the night of the twenty-fourth; it does not matter if you perform it on both nights. The narration returns to Muhammad ibn Muslim regarding ghusl: on the days of the two Eids, upon entering the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), on the day of entering Ihram, on the day of visitation, on the day one enters the House, on the day of Tarwiah, on the day of Arafat, ghusl for the deceased, and when one washes and shrouds the deceased or touches them after they cool, on Friday, and ghusl for the solar eclipse if the disk is fully consumed and one wakes up and has not prayed, then one should perform ghusl and make up the prayer.
ai.seo_question: What are the seventeen occasions requiring ghusl according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these seventeen occasions into lunar nights, specific days, and physical states, reflecting the Shia emphasis on aligning ritual purity with cosmic and historical milestones. Notably, the inclusion of the 17th, 19th, 21st, and 23rd nights of Ramadan highlights their significance in Shia tradition as key nights for prayer and the potential occurrence of Laylat al-Qadr, while the mention of entering the Harams underscores the sanctity of the physical spaces of worship.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 17-1 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Hurayz ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, on the authority of Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB), “One should make major ritual ablutions (ghusl) for seventeen occasions: 1. On the night of the 17th of Ramazan which is the night on which the army of Islam encountered the army of Quraysh in the Battle of Badr. 2. On the night of the 19th of Ramazan on which one’s destiny is recorded. 3. On the night of the 21st of Ramazan on which the Trustees of the Prophets have died, Jesus - the son of Mary (MGB) was raised up to Heaven and Moses (MGB) died. 4. The night of the 23rd of Ramazan which is hoped to be the Night of Power. In another tradition narrated by Abdurrahman Ibn Aba Abdullah Basry we read that he had heard Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say, “You should also make major ritual ablutions (ghusl) on the night of the 24th of Ramazan. It is best to perform the major ritual ablutions (ghusl) on both nights.” Now returning to the tradition above narrated by Muhammad ibn Muslim, on the authority of Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB):

6- On the day of Eid ul-Azha.7- On the day of Eid ul-Fitr. 8 and 9 - Upon entering the shrines in Mecca and Medina. 10- On the day of wearing the Ihram (Taharrum). 11- On the pilgrimage day. 12- On the day of entering the House of God. 13- On the day of Al-Tarviat. 14- On the day of Arafat. 15- Upon performing the major ritual ablutions (ghusl) for the deceased. Once you perform the major ritual ablutions (ghusl) for the deceased and shroud the corpse, or when you touch the corpse after if gets cold. 16- On Fridays. 17- If on total eclipse of the sun you wake up and you had not said the prayers for the eclipse of the sun, then you should make major ritual ablutions (ghusl) and say the prayers.
